summary: Unbalanced healthcheck latency evicts model pin during quiet canary rollout
description:
Issue summary: During a low-traffic canary rollout for redwood-open-7b-v2 in us-east-1 for BrightWriter Inc. we observed ephemeral loss of model pinning for a subset of tenant sessions. The system evicted pins after a flurry of slow healthcheck responses from edge-proxy, causing ~15% of canary cohort traffic to fall back to the baseline variant. This affected deterministic behavior for pinned sessions and resulted in inconsistent model outputs for customer requests.

Impact: Partial incorrect model routing for BrightWriter’s dedicated cluster. Customer reported unexpected mixed responses (both new canary variant and baseline) for the same session within a short time window. No data loss, but correctness and SLA-impacting latency spikes for affected requests.
impact: ~15% of BrightWriter canary cohort experienced fallback to baseline model for 18 minutes; higher tail latency for pinned sessions; customer reported confusion in test harness and flagged production discrepancies.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer starts a canary rollout (20% weight) for redwood-open-7b-v2 on dedicated pool in us-east-1.
2) Send low QPS steady-state test traffic with session-affinity headers (tenant_id + session_token) to exercise pin behavior.
3) Observe that after a few minutes of successful pinned routing, a subset of sessions receive fallback responses and pin metadata shows evicted status at edge-proxy.
4) Replaying requests from captured IDs reproduces mixed-model outputs intermittently until pin rebind occurs.
Notes: Reproduction is timing-sensitive and more likely with QPS < 1 req/s per session and when healthchecks on edge-proxy spike above 350ms.
investigation_notes: Initial triage by CS: customer-provided traces show session affinity tokens still valid; pin metadata indicated 'evicted' within edge-proxy cache TTL window.

SRE hypothesis A: edge-proxy healthcheck latency spikes triggered an eviction path in the pin reconciler which treats slow health probes as node unhealthy and clears local pin maps (defensive eviction).
SRE hypothesis B: a race between canary-coordinator promote window and pin-lease-renewal for low QPS sessions caused re-evaluation of pin eligibility and eviction as a side-effect.

Correlation: healthcheck rolling_p90 correlated with the start of evictions (see grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/serving/edge-health?from=2026-03-10T02:00:00Z&to=2026-03-10T02:40:00Z).
Edge team found recent change in edge-proxy PR 302 (timeout/backoff tweak) that increases probe backoff jitter; may amplify transient slow probes under low load. PR linked above.
Reproduction by Eng: locally reproduced by artificially increasing probe latency to 400ms while keeping session QPS < 1; pin reconciler moved sessions to fallback within 2-3 probe cycles.

Risk: Customers with low per-session QPS are more likely to have pins evicted during noisy probe windows; since evictions are defensive the system recovers but can cause brief inconsistency for pinned sessions.
Workaround tested: lengthen pin lease TTL on the dedicated pool for BrightWriter (-experimental flag) or increase canary weight temporarily to keep more active sessions on target nodes.

Proposed fix: adjust reconciler logic to require N consecutive health-failing probes before evicting a pin when session QPS < threshold; add telemetry to track eviction reasons per-tenant. Engineering ticket created.
resolution: Temporary workaround applied for BrightWriter at 2026-03-11 04:00Z: increased pin lease TTL for the customer’s dedicated pool and bumped canary weight to 30% for 1 hour to stabilize pins. Long-term fix in progress: change pin reconciler to 3-strike policy for healthcheck-induced evictions in low-QPS cohorts. PR reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1794 (in review). Follow-ups: postmortem and instrumentation task assigned to SRE (INT-3402).
